hierarchy: Dataset -> Graph / construction -> Search run -> Measurements

avg_dist_cmps.availability: When reported by the native search tool.
avg_dist_cmps.definition: Average distance computations per query; for this data it is the one query's count.

build_time_s.availability: When the construction timing is available.
build_time_s.definition: Active construction time for the graph searched by this row.

candidates_generated.availability: Only when the native search binary records it explicitly.
candidates_generated.definition: Candidate count emitted by the native search binary.

epsilon_recall_0_01.availability: Only when per-query returned and exact distances are available.
epsilon_recall_0_01.definition: Fraction of queries whose nearest returned distance is within 1.01 times the exact nearest-neighbor distance.

epsilon_recall_0_1.availability: Only when per-query returned and exact distances are available.
epsilon_recall_0_1.definition: Fraction of queries whose nearest returned distance is within 1.1 times the exact nearest-neighbor distance.

index_size_bytes.availability: Always for a complete persisted index.
index_size_bytes.definition: Total on-disk bytes of all persisted files belonging to the searched index prefix.

max_extra_expanded_after_returned_top_10.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_extra_expanded_after_returned_top_10.definition: Maximum per-query number of additional expansions after all returned top-10 nodes had already been expanded, using the returned nodes' expanded orders.
max_extra_expanded_after_returned_top_10.display_label: Max extra expanded after top-10 expanded

max_extra_seen_after_returned_top_10_see.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_extra_seen_after_returned_top_10_see.definition: Maximum per-query number of additional seen nodes after all returned top-10 nodes had already been first seen, using the returned nodes' first-seen orders.
max_extra_seen_after_returned_top_10_see.display_label: Max extra seen after top-10 seen

max_preceding_expanded_count_at_1.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_preceding_expanded_count_at_1.definition: Maximum, over measured queries, of how many nodes were expanded before the returned rank-1 result was expanded. Null per query if the returned node was not expanded before termination.

max_preceding_expanded_count_top_10.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_preceding_expanded_count_top_10.definition: Maximum, over measured queries and returned top-10 results, of how many nodes were expanded before that returned result was expanded. Null per query if the returned node was not expanded before termination.

max_preceding_visited_count_at_1.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_preceding_visited_count_at_1.definition: Maximum, over measured queries, of how many nodes were first seen before the returned rank-1 result. First-seen order is recorded by the native search trace.

max_preceding_visited_count_top_10.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_preceding_visited_count_top_10.definition: Maximum, over measured queries and returned top-10 results, of how many nodes were first seen before that returned result.

max_total_expanded_count.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_total_expanded_count.definition: Maximum per-query number of nodes popped/expanded by the search. For centroid search, repeated branch-local expansions are counted as work.

max_total_seen_count.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
max_total_seen_count.definition: Maximum per-query number of nodes first seen/inserted into the candidate pool by the search. For centroid search, repeated branch-local discoveries are counted as work.

mean_extra_expanded_after_returned_top_1.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
mean_extra_expanded_after_returned_top_1.definition: Mean number of additional expansions after all returned top-10 nodes had already been expanded, using the returned nodes' expanded orders.
mean_extra_expanded_after_returned_top_1.display_label: Mean extra expanded after top-10 expanded

mean_extra_seen_after_returned_top_10_se.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
mean_extra_seen_after_returned_top_10_se.definition: Mean number of additional seen nodes after all returned top-10 nodes had already been first seen, using the returned nodes' first-seen orders.
mean_extra_seen_after_returned_top_10_se.display_label: Mean extra seen after top-10 seen

mean_latency_us.definition: Mean warm-up-free search latency; for this single-query data it is that one query's latency.

mean_total_expanded_count.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
mean_total_expanded_count.definition: Mean number of nodes popped/expanded by the search. For centroid search, repeated branch-local expansions are counted as work.

mean_total_seen_count.availability: Only for searches rerun with query trace metrics enabled.
mean_total_seen_count.definition: Mean number of nodes first seen/inserted into the candidate pool by the search. For centroid search, repeated branch-local discoveries are counted as work.

p50_latency_us.definition: 50th percentile of warm-up-free individual query timings.

p95_latency_us.definition: 95th percentile of warm-up-free individual query timings.

p999_latency_us.definition: 99.9th percentile of warm-up-free individual query timings.

p99_latency_us.definition: 99th percentile of warm-up-free individual query timings.

qps.availability: Workload or repeated-single-query measurements only; omitted for single_query.
qps.definition: Measured-query count divided by measured-search wall time.

recall.definition: Percentage of the top-K ground-truth neighbors returned.

recall_at_10.definition: Recall calculated against the ten nearest ground-truth neighbors.

recall_at_5.definition: Recall calculated against the five nearest ground-truth neighbors.

relative_error.availability: Only when per-query returned and exact distances are available.
relative_error.definition: Mean nearest-returned distance divided by the exact nearest-neighbor distance, calculated per query.

query_measurement_definitions.batch_mode: Whether the native search executed a query batch.
query_measurement_definitions.latency_sample_count: Warm-up-free individual timings available for latency summaries.
query_measurement_definitions.measured_query_count: Number of searches represented by the measurement.
query_measurement_definitions.percentile_method: Named method used for emitted percentiles, otherwise null.
query_measurement_definitions.unique_query_count: Number of distinct query vectors represented.
query_measurement_definitions.warmup_query_count: Warm-up searches excluded from reported metrics.

question:
Question: How do the same Paper-fast graph and its shortcut augmentation trade
recall for latency across greedy, full-centroid, and 50%-partial-centroid search?

scope.gist1m: fresh Paper-fast construction plus serial halving-shortcut graph derived from that exact base
scope.sift1m_direct_shortcuts: threshold-direct shortcut graph derived from the same exported SIFT1M Paper-fast graph
scope.sift1m_reversed_shortcuts_1: reverse-order shortcut graph derived from the same exported SIFT1M Paper-fast graph, starting from expanded-order node 1
scope.sift1m_shortcuts: derived from the exported SIFT1M Paper-fast graph
scope.sift1m_while_direct_shortcuts: while-direct shortcut graph derived from the same exported SIFT1M Paper-fast graph; repeated passes recheck only targets that remained longer than the threshold
